q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
q.e: Vertical, horizontal and both diagonals — four folds give matching halves.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle (not a square) have?
q.e: Only the two lines through the middles of opposite sides. Its diagonals are NOT lines of symmetry.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
q.e: One from each corner to the middle of the opposite side.

q.t: A line of symmetry divides a figure into two parts that …
o: match exactly when folded along the line
q.e: Each half is the mirror image of the other.

q.t: Which has NO line of symmetry?
q.e: Nothing in a cloud repeats in a regular way.

q.t: A pinwheel looks the same after a quarter turn. This is called …
q.e: Looking the same after turning about a centre is rotational symmetry.

q.t: Which angle is an angle of symmetry for EVERY figure?
q.e: A full turn always brings any figure back to where it started.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
q.e: Every line through the centre is a line of symmetry.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
q.e: A regular polygon with n sides has n lines of symmetry.

q.t: Paper folded once and punched once. How many holes when opened?
q.e: One fold makes two layers, and the punch goes through both.

q.t: What are the angles of symmetry of a square?
q.e: A quarter turn makes a square look the same, and so do 2, 3 and 4 quarter turns.

q.t: What is the order of rotational symmetry of an equilateral triangle?
q.e: Angles 120°, 240°, 360° — three of them.

q.t: What is the smallest angle of symmetry of a rectangle (not a square)?
q.e: Only a half turn (and a full turn) makes a rectangle look the same.

q.t: Paper folded twice (in half, then in half again) and punched once. How many holes?
q.e: Each fold doubles the layers: 2 × 2 = 4.

q.t: Why is a rectangle's diagonal not a line of symmetry?
o: When folded along it, the corners stick out and the halves don't match
Diagonals are never lines of symmetry
It is — it splits it into equal halves
q.e: The two triangles are equal but don't land on each other when folded — unless it's a square.

q.t: A figure with 5 evenly spaced arms — what is its smallest angle of symmetry?
q.e: Each turn must carry one arm onto the next: 360° ÷ 5 = 72°.

q.t: Which triangle has exactly one line of symmetry?
q.e: The line runs from the corner between the equal sides to the middle of the third side.

q.t: Can a triangle have exactly 2 lines of symmetry?
o: No — two lines force all sides equal, which gives a third line
q.e: A triangle has 0, 1 or 3 lines of symmetry.

q.t: Reflect square ABCD in its diagonal AC. What happens to A and C?
o: They move to B and D
q.e: Points on the fold line don't move; B and D swap.

q.t: A figure's smallest angle of symmetry is 60°. Which is also an angle of symmetry?
q.e: Angles of symmetry are multiples of the smallest: 60, 120, 180, 240, 300, 360.

q.t: A figure's smallest angle of symmetry is 45°. What is its order of rotational symmetry?
Can a figure's smallest angle of symmetry be 17°?
o: No — 17 is not a factor of 360
q.e: The smallest angle (in whole degrees) must divide 360 exactly; 360 ÷ 17 isn't whole.

q.t: 60° is an angle of symmetry and there are two smaller angles of symmetry. What is the smallest?
q.e: The angles are multiples of the smallest, and 60° is the 3rd one: 60 ÷ 3 = 20°.

q.t: A figure has 7 evenly spaced arms. What is its smallest angle of symmetry?
q.e: 360 ÷ 7 = 51 remainder 3, so 51 3/7° — not a whole number.

q.t: What are the lines-of-symmetry numbers for regular polygons from triangle to decagon?
q.e: A regular polygon has as many lines of symmetry as sides: the counting numbers from 3.

q.t: Which quadrilateral has rotational symmetry but NO line of symmetry?
o: A parallelogram that isn't a rectangle or rhombus
q.e: It looks the same after a half turn but no fold makes its halves match.

q.t: Which quadrilateral has a line of symmetry but no rotational symmetry?
q.e: A kite folds along its long diagonal, but no turn under 360° brings it back.

q.t: A circle is cut into 12 equal sectors and coloured to have exactly 4 angles of symmetry. How many sectors are in the repeating pattern?
q.e: The pattern repeats 4 times round 12 sectors: 12 ÷ 4 = 3.

q.t: The outer boundary of the new Parliament building has rotational symmetry. What are its angles of symmetry?
q.e: It is triangle-like with 3 lines of symmetry and turns onto itself every 120°.

q.t: A regular hexagon's angles of symmetry are multiples of …
A circle of 12 equal sectors is coloured in a repeating pattern. Which number of angles of symmetry is IMPOSSIBLE?
q.e: The pattern must repeat a whole number of times round 12 sectors, so the count must divide 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does every Koch snowflake after the first (triangle) have?
q.e: The bumps make it look the same from six directions: 6 lines, and angles of symmetry every 60°.

q.t: Which statement is true for every figure?
o: If the smallest angle of symmetry is a whole number of degrees, it is a factor of 360
Every figure has a line of symmetry
Every figure has order at least 2
The smallest angle of symmetry is always 90°
q.e: Repeating the smallest turn must land exactly on a full turn of 360°.

q.t: Which triangle has at least 2 lines AND at least 2 angles of symmetry?
q.e: Only the equilateral triangle: 3 lines and angles 120°, 240°, 360°.

q.t: Paper is folded in half twice and the closed corner is cut off with a straight slanting cut. What hole appears when opened?
o: A diamond — a square standing on its corner
q.e: The slanting cut is reflected across both folds, making four equal edges around the centre.

q.t: An opened paper shows 4 holes, symmetric about a vertical and a horizontal line. How was it folded before one punch?
o: In half vertically and then horizontally
q.e: Two folds make 4 layers; the hole pattern shows both fold lines as lines of symmetry.

q.t: A figure has rotational symmetry of order 9. What is its smallest angle of symmetry?
How many lines of symmetry does a regular 12-sided polygon have?
q.e: A regular n-gon has n lines: 6 through opposite corners and 6 through middles of opposite sides.

q.t: Three arms meet at a centre at angles 100°, 120°, 140°. What is its order of rotational symmetry?
q.e: The gaps are unequal, so no turn less than a full turn carries every arm onto another.

q.t: On squared paper a corner is 3 squares left of the line of symmetry. Where is its reflection?
o: 3 squares right of the line, level with it
q.e: A reflection puts each point the same distance from the line on the other side, straight across.
